Create a new Risk game state

Source: R/game.R
rk_game.Rd

Constructs an rk_game object holding the players, territory ownership and army counts, the map, and whose turn it is. Territories are dealt out at random and each player then spreads their starting armies over the territories they hold (40 armies for two players, 35 for three, and so on down to 20 for six, as in the printed rules). The default map is the classic 42-territory world (see rk_world()).

Usage

rk_game(players, map = rk_world(), seed = NULL)

Arguments

players

Character vector of 2 to 6 unique player names.

map

An rk_map object. Defaults to rk_world().

seed

Optional whole number seed for the random deal. Supplying it calls set.seed() and therefore resets the caller's random number stream.

Value

An S3 object of class rk_game: a list with elements

players

character, the roster in turn order (never changes).

active

character, the players who still hold territory.

map

the rk_map being played on.

state

a tibble::tibble() with one row per territory and columns territory (character), owner (character) and armies (integer), in map order.

turn

character, the player to move.

phase

character, one of "reinforce", "attack", "fortify" or "over".

round

integer, the current round, starting at 1.

fortified

a flag: has the player to move already fortified?

last_battle

the rk_battle most recently resolved; an empty battle before the first attack.

log

a tibble::tibble() of actions with columns round (integer), player, action, from, to (character), armies (integer) and conquered (logical).

See also

rk_reinforce(), rk_attack(), rk_fortify() and rk_end_turn() for the turn cycle, and rk_play() to run a whole game.

Other game: rk_armies(), rk_continents_held(), rk_is_winner(), rk_owner(), rk_reinforcements(), rk_territories(), rk_winner(), summary.rk_game()

Examples

game <- rk_game(c("Red", "Blue", "Green"), seed = 1)
game
#> <rk_game> 3 players on 42 territories, round 1
#> Turn: Red (reinforce phase)
#> * Red: 14 territories, 35 armies, 0 continents
#>   Blue: 14 territories, 35 armies, 0 continents
#>   Green: 14 territories, 35 armies, 0 continents
summary(game)
#> # A tibble: 3 × 6
#>   player territories armies continents reinforcements alive
#>   <chr>        <int>  <int>      <int>          <int> <lgl>
#> 1 Red             14     35          0              4 TRUE 
#> 2 Blue            14     35          0              4 TRUE 
#> 3 Green           14     35          0              4 TRUE
